prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which bifunctional PROTAC molecules induce proximity between a target protein and an E3 ubiquitin ligase to destroy it

statement.case_for: My first-round position stands: B068 with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, with the citation narrowed to the PROTAC concept and its chemical underpinnings. After the first-round exchange I find the case rests on three things that the other shortlisted candidates do not combine. First, the mechanism is defined at molecular level: a ternary complex between target, degrader and E3 ligase, with crystal structures and measurable cooperativity, so this is understood chemistry and not only a phenotype. Second, it is a design principle (event-driven, catalytic pharmacology) that lets chemists address proteins without a druggable pocket, and it has been reproduced across many targets and E3 ligases by independent groups. Third, it has become a routine tool for acute, reversible protein depletion in cell biology and a large clinical pipeline, which is the test I apply when asking whether a discovery changed what researchers and clinicians can do. Seven of eight members place B068 in their first choice or alternatives, which I do not treat as a substitute for the science, but it does suggest the concept is not seen as parochial. Ciulli stays as the third name because the structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex work made the approach rational and general; I considered Sakamoto (first author of the 2001 proof of principle) and Handa, but a PROTAC-focused citation is best served by the person who turned the concept into a design discipline.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC drug is approved, so 2026 may be early and a late-stage failure would weaken the prize. The cereblon and thalidomide molecular-glue lineage (Handa, Ito, Kim, Sakamoto, Gray) has a distinct origin and the strongest link to approved drugs, and a PROTAC-only citation leaves it out. Three names also exclude Sakamoto, whose 2001 first authorship has a real claim, and Gray, Bradner and others in the later small-molecule era. If the committee puts reproducibility and clean attribution first, B003 or B009 are more mature and B004 has far less attribution risk. I cannot fully resolve the one-lineage-or-two question inside a single three-person citation.

responses.point: A PROTAC-only trio omits the part of the field with the most patient benefit, the cereblon molecular-glue lineage, and Handa or Sakamoto could be the third name instead of Ciulli.
responses.response: This is the strongest objection to our shared configuration and I take it seriously. I still think the two lineages are separable in a citation: PROTACs are rationally designed heterobifunctional molecules, while thalidomide and its analogues were discovered as drugs and their cereblon mechanism was found afterwards, so the design principle that I value belongs to the PROTAC line. I accept that this wording leaves Handa and the glue chemists for a later prize or a second part, and I would not claim the citation covers the clinical benefit of immunomodulatory drugs. On the third name, I keep Ciulli because the 2001 concept is already carried by Crews and Deshaies and Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex work made the approach general; Sakamoto's claim is real but is mostly the early proof of principle.

responses.point: B003 gives a sharp dated origin (2009 P-granule droplets, Rosen's 2012 reconstitution) and generative reach, and the physical-chemical principle can be separated from contested in vivo claims.
responses.response: I agree that B003 has the broadest support apart from B068 and that the principle of multivalent demixing is real physical chemistry. My difficulty is the chair's own question: a citation that avoids asserting in vivo phase separation would be a statement about in vitro demixing, and the field's reach depends exactly on the in vivo claims that remain argued case by case. A prize for the principle alone risks being both safe and unsatisfying, while degradation is validated directly in cells and animals. I would move to B003 if the committee wanted a physical-chemistry prize and judged that PROTAC clinical validation is too incomplete, but I do not think that is yet the better scientific judgment. I also doubt Rosen over Pappu is settled, which adds to the attribution risk.

responses.point: Base editing (B024) is a conceptually simple chemical tool with tractable attribution under Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, though close to 2020 and with an open Target-AID priority question.
responses.response: I appreciate that you hold your own case to a high standard, and your point that the short clinical record, 2020 overlap and Kondo/Nishida priority are open is what keeps me from ranking B024 above B068. I accept your argument that attribution is cleaner than for degraders, and that edited patients are already reported, which weakens my own argument about clinical timing. The chemistry is the deamination, but the invention that made it work was protein engineering built on a technology already honoured in 2020, so the chemical novelty seems to me narrower than for a small-molecule design principle. I would pair B024 with prime editing in a later year, as you suggest.

responses.point: Nitrogenase (B009) is a well-defined, independently confirmed structural and mechanistic achievement, though the N2 reduction mechanism is still unsettled and credit is crowded.
responses.response: I agree that B009 is more mature than B068 and has a clearer atomic-level story. The two questions you and Zou raise about the unresolved catalytic mechanism and the choice among Dean, Einsle and Ribbe are exactly why I hesitate: a structure-and-cofactor citation is defensible, but a mechanism-based one is not, and any trio omits someone with a serious claim. For the criterion I use, whether a discovery changed what other researchers and clinicians can do, nitrogenase has fewer downstream tools, though I acknowledge its link to ammonia synthesis. I would rank it clearly above B004 and B023 as a fallback on maturity grounds.

uncertainties: Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC drug makes 2026 too early; I would reconsider if late-stage results were negative.
Whether PROTACs and molecular glues are one lineage or two, and whether a second prize part would be better than a PROTAC-only citation.
Whether Ciulli, Sakamoto or Handa is the right third name, which I cannot resolve from my own knowledge of the primary literature.
What evidence would move me to a fallback: a clear majority judgment that maturity and clean attribution should outweigh conceptual reach would move me to B003, then B009.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any credited candidate. My postdoc mentors (Molly Stevens, Freddy Boey) are not credited on any shortlisted ballot. My research overlap with Emma Sparr on peptide self-assembly is not a recusal matter, and I note that she and Heiner Linke both prefer B003. I co-founded a biosensor company but it has no connection to PROTACs or any shortlisted candidate. Nothing has changed since round 1.
